relevance_note: Case series of nine Chinese patients with Danon disease, all with LAMP2 p.Leu325fs frameshift variants, with per-participant tables: "A total of nine participants with confirmed DD were included, all carrying LAMP2 p.Leu325fs variants".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script (scratch only) transcribed Table 1 (cDNA, protein, ACMG, +/− rows, chief complaint), Table 2 (cells marked ↑), Table 3 (cells marked ↑/↓ and ECG cells = 1) and Table 4 (P1–P8 rows), and I checked its output against the tables; every span was then checked verbatim by script. Labels: the paper uses "P1"–"P9" in all tables and "Participant 1"–"Participant 9" in text; the P-form is the more frequent and is used. Table 1 has patients as columns, with P3, P4 and P9 each spanning two columns (repeated header "P3 | P3" etc.; the two columns differ only in the family-history rows); spans quote the row through the participant's first column (P1=col1, P2=2, P3=3, P4=5, P5=7, P6=8, P7=9, P8=10, P9=11; family-history second columns 4, 6, 12). Table 1 column header for genetics is "Molecular Genetics (LAMP2, NMNM_002294.3)" (sic). Age at diagnosis taken as the second number of the Table 1 cell "Age: 1st visit / diagnosis (y)" (e.g. 21.5/24 -> 24); this is a two-field cell defined by its row label, not a stacked multi-patient cell. Age at first visit, diagnostic delay and Table 3 "Age at the most Severe Symptoms" were not recorded (no matching field). Table symbols: Table 1 "+, present; −, absent" is defined in the legend, so "−" for skeletal myopathy, cognitive impairment and ocular manifestation is recorded excluded. Table 3 ECG rows use 1/0, which the legend does not define: 1 recorded observed (counts match the text), 0 left not reported. Table 3 MR/TR "−" cells left not reported because the legend defines "−-, no regurgitation", not "−". ↑/↓ arrows are not defined in legends; ↑ in Table 2 read against the reference range printed in the row label. Lab values within range without a statement of normality were not recorded as excluded; only "CK remained within the normal range in all five female participants" was used (elevated CK excluded for P1, P3, P7, P8, P9). Checklist: "Cognitive impairment −" does not exclude the composite item "intellectual disability, cognitive impairment or learning difficulties" (left not reported); "Ocular manifestation −" excludes only ocular manifestation, so myopia and retinopathy are not reported for everyone (the text says three had visual impairment, two bilateral refractive error and one bilateral strabismus, without naming them). Heart failure left not reported for all (NYHA classes recorded as features; MACCE and heart-failure statements are unnamed). Elevated EDVi on cardiac MR (P6, P7, P8) was not used for the "dilated LV" checklist item; that item uses echo LV↑/EF↓. Scope: nine participants plus relatives described as affected or tested: father of P1 (died of heart disease), mother of P3 (HCM, deceased; same person as P4's "Grandmother" in Table 1), and for P9 the younger brother (carrier, DD and DCM), mother (HCM, deceased, not genotyped), and father, aunt and daughter (tested, did not carry: "only her younger brother carried this hemizygous variant site"). P1's grandmother (died in her forties, cause unconfirmed, not tested) was left out as neither affected nor tested. The younger brother's variant row uses P9's c.974del / p.Leu325ArgfsTer21 because the paper says he carries "this hemizygous variant site"; transcript, type and classification are left not reported for him. P4 inheritance recorded maternal: P3 and P4 are mother and son and both carry c.973dup in Table 1. Contradictions and discrepancies in the paper: (1) Abstract says "All participants carried pathogenic frameshift variants" but Table 1 classifies c.973del and c.974del (P5–P9) as Likely pathogenic; table values recorded. (2) P4: text and cardiac MR call him HCM (IVS 33↑, LVMi 174↑; chief complaint HOCM; biopsy hypertrophy) but echo shows IVST 10↓, LVPWT 10↓ and the text groups him with "relatively thin posterior walls, corresponding to their dilated cardiomyopathy phenotype"; Table 1 also lists P3 (his mother) as "DD and DCM" and P4 as "DD and HCM". Both sets of rows emitted; the LVH checklist item is not reported for P4. (3) P3 is called DCM in text and Table 1 but "HCM (End-stage)" on cardiac MR and non-obstructive HCM with LV dilation at pathology; both rows emitted. (4) P4 and P5 have reduced EF on echo (25↓, 32↓) but LVEF 56 and 50 on cardiac MR, where the six non-end-stage HCM participants are said to have preserved LVEF; dilated/hypokinetic LV recorded observed from echo (LV 71↑ and 53↑). (5) Text says hs-cTnI elevated in "five of the six participants with available data" but Table 2 marks all six available values ↑; table recorded. (6) Text says six had increased IVS thickness and four increased LV diameter; Table 3 marks five ↑ for each. (7) Text says six had chest tightness and three decreased exercise tolerance; Table 1 lists CP for seven and fatigue for five. (8) P5 CK-MB 4.8 is above the printed range 0.3–4.0 but not marked ↑ and the text counts six elevated (without P5); not recorded. P8 Mb 67.9 lacks ↑ but the text names P8 as elevated; recorded from text. (9) One heart-transplant recipient (unnamed; P3 is one of the two) developed persistent skeletal muscle weakness after transplant, while Table 1 marks skeletal myopathy "−" for all but P9; not assigned to anyone. Vital status recorded only for the two named deaths (P6, P9); the others were not marked alive although only two of nine died. The "prior genetic analysis of 42 confirmed patients" is not cited as a publication, so cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is null.
